logline: A young aspiring knight races across a treacherous kingdom to deliver a secret letter to a distant king - a quest based on the beloved Dutch children's classic by Tonke Dragt.

Unambitious family fare that tries to piggyback on the success of Game of Thrones.

seasons.review_body: Netflix's adaptation of Tonke Dragt's 1962 Dutch classic arrived in March 2020 with a 55-percent Rotten Tomatoes score across 22 reviews - a mixed-to-middling verdict that mirrored audience sentiment. Critics who responded favourably highlighted the young cast's commitment and the lush European location photography; detractors pointed to bloated pacing, a tone caught between children's adventure and adult fantasy, and liberties taken with the source text that drew a pointed rebuke from Dutch audiences. The IMDb score settled at 6.0. The series is engaging when it focuses on Tiuri's moral dilemmas and cross-cultural friendships, but the six-episode runtime strains a premise that works better as a compact novel. Fans of the book will find the changes divisive; newcomers will get a competent, sometimes charming, but rarely memorable quest narrative.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes Tiuri as an earnest underdog on the eve of his knighthood vigil before a chance encounter sets a continent-spanning quest in motion. The Dutch-English production design is handsome and the young lead likeable, even if the plotting leans on well-worn fantasy conventions.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Tiuri makes a fateful choice inside the church vigil that costs him everything - and defines the entire series.
